title: DOW-UAP-D091, Range Fouler Debrief, Atlantic Ocean, 2020
what_is_it: A completed U.S. Navy Range Fouler Debrief form — a standardised report filed by an aircrew member documenting an unauthorised object intruding into controlled airspace during operations.
core_summary: A Navy aircrew member (a Weapons Systems Officer, rank O-3) filed a Range Fouler Debrief describing an object seen while operating in controlled airspace over the Atlantic Ocean in 2020. The object was reported as a darker, maroonish colour, roughly 12-15 feet tall, and structurally resembling a large, somewhat deformed balloon. After the observation the aircrew proceeded back to the ship and landed without incident.
interpretation_warnings: Single-source, subjective observer account; descriptions reflect the reporter's interpretation at the time, not a verified determination of the object's nature.

The form is heavily redacted — identifying information (aircrew, squadron) is deliberately sanitised, and much of the narrative, coordinates, date, time and repository details are obscured or garbled by OCR.

Key fields (exact date, latitude/longitude, altitude, movement, wind data) are blank or unreadable in the extracted text, so the incident cannot be independently located or timed from this document alone.
Incident location (Atlantic Ocean) and year (2020) come from the war.gov metadata, not from legible body text.
The observation is consistent with a balloon per the observer's own description, but the report itself draws no conclusion about what the object was.
